title: U.S. House · Kansas's 3rd District
area: Northeast Kansas, mainly Wyandotte and Johnson Counties (Kansas City, KS and its suburbs)

context.text: Incumbent Sharice Davids (D) defeated primary challenger Sarah Preu, 83.4% to 16.6%, in her first contested primary since being elected in 2018. Eric Jenkins, a retired Army colonel and former Shawnee City Council member, defeated Chase LaPorte in the Republican primary after filing near the June 1 deadline. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is D+2, the most competitive of Kansas's four districts.

summary.text: Sharice Davids is the Democratic incumbent representing Kansas's 3rd District since 2019. A member of the Ho-Chunk Nation and former mixed-martial-arts fighter, she previously worked in economic development on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation and as a White House Fellow before running for Congress.

background.text: Earned an associate degree from Johnson County Community College (2003), a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Missouri-Kansas City (2007), and a law degree from Cornell Law School (2010).

Worked as a White House Fellow in the Department of Transportation, chair of the board of Twelve Clans, Inc. for the Ho-Chunk Nation, deputy director for the Thunder Valley Community Development Corporation on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, and director of economic development at Red Cloud Indian School.
Is a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation and competed professionally in mixed martial arts (1-1 record).
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018, succeeding Kevin Yoder.

priorities.text: Filed for a fifth term casting herself as a check on what she called "extremism" in Washington, D.C.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Conservation, Research, and Biotechnology; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit) and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit), 2025-2026 assignments.

candidates.name: Eric Jenkins
candidates.currentRole: Former Shawnee City Council member (two terms, Ward 2)

summary.text: Eric Jenkins is a retired U.S. Army colonel and former Shawnee, Kansas city councilmember who won the Republican nomination against Chase LaPorte after filing near the June 1 deadline, running on fiscal responsibility, lower taxes, and border security.

background.text: Retired as a colonel in the U.S. Army after 30 years of service.
Spent 28 years in Shawnee, Kansas city government, including on the Shawnee Planning Commission and two terms on the city council representing Ward 2, before losing his 2023 reelection bid.
Announced his congressional campaign on May 22, 2026, close to Kansas's June 1 filing deadline.

priorities.text: Campaign platform focuses on fiscal responsibility, lowering taxes for families and Kansas businesses, and strong border security and national defense.

Says he is running to fight for safer communities, lower costs, secure borders, and accountable government, and criticizes Davids for backing Biden-era policy and opposing Trump administration border and public-safety efforts.
priorities.quote: Sharice Davids spent years backing the Biden-Harris agenda that drove up costs, weakened our economy, and failed to secure the border.

positions.summary: Campaigns on strong border security and supports the Trump administration's border enforcement efforts.

candidates.researchNotes: Jenkins has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions drawn from a Johnson County Post news report citing his campaign announcement and website.

candidates.name: Steve Hohe

summary.text: Steve Hohe is a retired U.S. Air Force veteran and businessman running as the Libertarian Party candidate.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1980 to 1991.
Earned an associate degree from the Community College of the Air Force (1991) and a bachelor's degree from Husson College (1992); worked as a businessman.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or public statements on policy issues found; background is limited to Ballotpedia's biographical summary. He has not completed the Candidate Connection survey.
